title: Northwood Guardian - private onramp & egress scenario discussion
next_steps: Redwood to send private deployment network checklist and sample diagram (Maya) by 2027-03-01
Customer to share current VPC CIDR ranges and peering constraints (Priya) by 2027-02-26
Schedule a deep-dive on Transit Gateway/Shared VPC setup with Derek and Arjun wk of 2027-03-07
Redwood SE to run a quick smoke benchmark in eu-west-1 vs us-east-1 and share latency/cost impacts (Arjun) by 2027-03-04
Security docs (SOC2 pack, KMS/HSM notes) to be emailed to Evan (Jordan) by 2027-02-25
action_items: Arjun Patel: draft CIDR collision checklist + recommended NAT architecture - due 2027-03-02
Priya Malhotra: export and send VPC/subnet, route table and firewall egress rules - due 2027-02-26
Maya Chen: share private deployment pricing baseline and Dedicated burst options - due 2027-02-25
Evan Ross: gather internal compliance questions for SOC2 + KMS usage - due 2027-03-01
summary: Initial technical discovery for private onramp. Customer running sensitive connected devices platform with strict egress/residency requirements. Main constraints: must keep traffic within EU regions for EU customers, minimal cross-account CIDR overlap, no public internet ingress to inference nodes, and audit logs + KMS-managed keys. Discussed options: Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane + private endpoints), Dedicated pools with VPC peering, and fallback hosted endpoints. Agreed to share network diagrams and run region latency checks.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-02-23 16:00 PST / Duration 47m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Evan, Priya, Derek, Lena, Tom (Northwood Guardian)
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining we got about 45 minutes, quick intros?
[00:12] Evan: evan ross security eng at northwood, we look after infra and compliance. sorry if i sound rough, juggling two things.
[00:20] Priya: priya, cloud architect, i'll lead the network bits.
[00:24] Derek: derek, network lead, i'll be nuts and bolts for peering and routing.
[00:29] Lena: lena product - interested in UX and latency targets.
[00:33] Tom: tom procurement, i'll handle contracting questions later.
[00:36] Maya: great, quick from our side arjun is our se, samira on solutions engineering for private onramp, jordan will own security docs.
[00:45] Arjun: hey team, quick agenda - clarify their constraints, map routing options (peering vs transit), private endpoint patterns (privatelink or equivalent), and any region gating. then next steps. sound good?
[00:55] Priya: yep, main thing - we operate multi-region eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for EU customers, us-east for NA. EU data must not leave EU for EU tenancy. Also we have on-prem datacenters that talk to cloud via express route / direct connect equivalents.
[01:10] Derek: we have overlapping CIDR ranges across some partners, so we try to avoid introducing new overlaps; our VPCs are mostly 10.0.0.0/16 and some /20s.
[01:18] Lena: latency target for inference is 120ms p95 to EU users, ideally 80ms.
[01:23] Maya: ok that's helpful — thank you. a couple clarifying q's: do you want a control plane completely inside your VPC, or is a private endpoint back to our control plane acceptable?
[01:35] Evan: security wants no public control plane endpoints for EU tenant data. so private endpoint preferred.
[01:41] Arjun: ok we support a few patterns — 1) Redwood Private with a control plane in your VPC (we ship a control plane that runs in your account/VPC), 2) Private with VPC peering and endpoint services (Privatelink style), and 3) Dedicated pools with peering for data plane only while control plane remains hosted. each has tradeoffs.
[01:58] Priya: can you spell out differences re: routing / egress? specifically how egress to model pulls and container images occurs.
[02:06] Samira: good call - in Private with control plane in your VPC, model artifacts and images are pulled using your NAT/egress path; we can also support pre-staging artifacts into an internal artifact repo so no outbound internet is needed. in the privatelink pattern the data plane still needs to reach model storage unless you stage it. Dedicated pools can be in a customer account or in Redwood-managed infra with private peering.
[02:30] Derek: so for privatelink we still have to allow outbound to our S3 buckets unless you provide them inside our VPC?
[02:36] Arjun: yes exactly - there's always some artifact/channel - we can do S3 VPC endpoints, or ship the artifacts to your S3 account, or mirror images to ECR in your account - options vary on ops burden.
[02:50] Priya: about peering — we have a Transit Gateway in eu-west-1, we'd prefer attaching a Redwood VGW or transit attachment instead of lots of / peering links. how does Redwood handle TGW?
[03:04] Arjun: we can peer into a TGW. typical pattern is a transit attachment from your TGW to our VPC (if we deploy into your account) or we stitch via a cloud provider transit in a partner account. there's some prep: route tables, NACLs, and you need to make sure CIDR doesn't conflict.
[03:19] Derek: route propagation and black hole detection are big for us - if a route disappears we need failover. do you support BGP-based failover?
[03:27] Maya: short answer: we can integrate with BGP when using direct connect or partner interconnect for on-prem paths; for pure cloud TGW peering we rely on cloud route propagation. arjun correct me if i'm wrong.
[03:37] Arjun: yep that's right; BGP only for physical interconnects. for cloud peering we push routes and rely on TGW best path. we also support multi-region fallbacks: if eu-west is constrained we can failover to eu-central but that may violate data residency, so it's policy-based.
[03:55] Evan: about audit and keys — we need KMS-managed keys and HSM-backed keys for workspace encryption. do you integrate with customer KMS?
[04:03] Jordan: yes we support customer-managed KMS for both secrets and encrypted model caches; in private deployments the control plane can be configured to use your KMS.
[04:12] Evan: ok and logs? we need audit logs in our SIEM, forwarded in near-real-time.
[04:16] Arjun: we can forward audit logs to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/StackDriver) using private endpoints, or push via a collector in your VPC. samira can share the log schema.
[04:26] Samira: i'll attach our SIEM mapping and recommended retention.
[04:30] Priya: region gating - we have customers on the financial side in DE, internal policy mandates eu data for those. can you restrict model hosting to a region?
[04:39] Maya: yes you can pin models to region and we have policies to restrict routing. however some model variants might not be available in all regions; we can do quantized variants in EU to save cost.
[04:52] Derek: IP planning - what IP ranges do you request on peering?
[04:56] Arjun: if we deploy into your account we consume an allocation from your CIDR you provide; for managed Dedicated we request a small /28 for endpoints and use cross-account peering for data plane; specifics depend on pattern.
[05:10] Priya: do you offer private endpoints similar to aws privatelink where the traffic never goes over internet?
[05:15] Arjun: yes we can provide ENI-backed endpoint services or PrivateLink style interfaces depending on cloud. for GCP we use VPC connector equivalents.
[05:24] Lena: from product side - what's the latency hit when using privatelink vs direct in the same VPC?
[05:29] Arjun: typically +5-15ms depending on region and peering hops. we'll run a quick synthetic from your EU clusters to compare.
[05:36] Derek: any port requirements outbound? say for health checks or metrics?
[05:40] Samira: primarily HTTPS 443 outbound for control plane/agent; data plane token exchange also 443; for uploads to S3 or ECR standard ports. we can provide a minimal allow-list.
[05:50] Evan: SSO - we want SAML with SCIM and RBAC. how tightly is identity integrated?
[05:55] Jordan: we integrate SAML SSO for console and API access, SCIM provisioning for users, and RBAC that can be synced to groups. for private install we can tie into your IdP via SAML over the private link.
[06:06] Priya: network egress accounting - we have strict egress cost budgeting. how do you surface token-level / per-route cost?
[06:13] Maya: Redwood Console will show token-level breakdown in hosted mode; in private we provide agent-level and route-level telemetry and we can send detailed billing exports. the Optimize tooling suggests batching/quantization to reduce egress.
[06:28] Tom: procurement - can you operate under our standard terms? we have a net-60 and SOC2 compliance clause.
[06:34] Maya: we can start with a pilot under a standard MSA with exceptions noted; we'll need legal review but Jordan will coordinate security pack.
[06:40] Derek: real-world constraint — some of our partner networks only allow peering via specific ASN ranges; can you present an ASN we advertise?
[06:48] Arjun: we can advertise a public ASN if we manage the interconnect; if we deploy inside your account you can advertise your ASN. we'll note that in the checklist.
[06:59] Priya: what about ingress prevention - we cannot allow internet-to-inference traffic. can you ensure agents are not publicly routable?
[07:06] Samira: yes agents run in private subnets with no public IP; health checks and agent heartbeats go over the private link.
[07:13] Evan: are there any known gotchas with Terraform or IaC we should watch?
[07:17] Arjun: we provide modules for terraform to stand up the private deployment; main gotchas: CIDR overlap, IAM role cross-account trust policy, and route table propagation ordering. also watch for NACL defaults that block ephemeral ports.
[07:31] Priya: can you share the Terraform modules?
[07:33] Maya: yes we'll send the module repo link and a quickstart doc.
[07:37] Lena: what about model updates - when you push a model, how is rollout handled? we can't have large egress spikes.
[07:44] Arjun: we support staged rollouts and delta updates; we can pre-stage models to your artifact repo and only deliver diffs. also we can throttle parallel pulls to control egress.
[07:56] Evan: security — any third-party dependencies that pull from public registries? we need SBOM.
[08:02] Jordan: we can provide SBOMs and explain our supply chain. for private we can suppress public pulls by mirroring images.
[08:11] Tom: rough timeline - if pilot starts mid-March what would ramp look like?
[08:16] Maya: typical pilot 4-6 weeks: week 1 network prep and private peering, week 2 control plane deploy and model pre-stage, week 3 integration and smoke tests; week 4-6 load tests and refinement.
[08:30] Priya: ok that sounds doable. Derek will coordinate TGW peering homework.
[08:35] Derek: noted. we'll prepare route tables and list of CIDRs.
[08:39] Arjun: i'll outline the TGW attachment steps and the minimal route table entries.
[08:44] Maya: quick recap — we will: 1) send network checklist and terraform modules, 2) customer shares VPC details, 3) schedule TGW deep-dive, 4) Jordan to push security pack. next meeting we'll be at implementation kickoff. agree?
[08:57] Evan: agreed.
[09:00] Lena: thanks all.
[09:02] Maya: thanks team, i’ll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[09:07] [meeting ends]
